artists.biography:
The Matt Berry Trio is a UK acid jazz ensemble featuring Matt Berry alongside long-time collaborators Phill Scragg and Graham Mann, marking the first album release under this trio name. The group was formed to contribute to Acid Jazz Records’ The Jazz Sessions series, delivering their debut album Everything’s Peachy, which was released on June 26, 2026, across multiple formats including black vinyl, a limited green vinyl exclusive to the Acid Jazz store, CD, digital download, and streaming platforms. The album is a 12-part instrumental suite that explores Berry’s diverse influences in jazz, modern classical, and electronic music, showcasing the trio’s tight interplay and experimental spirit.

Everything’s Peachy serves as the second volume in The Jazz Sessions series, following the successful debut Soul Drums by The Steve White Trio, and highlights the Matt Berry Trio’s unique position within the acid jazz scene. The project reflects Matt Berry’s decade-long association with Acid Jazz Records, a partnership that has seen him evolve into an extraordinary musician with a career spanning diverse musical adventures. With Everything’s Peachy, the trio not only continues Berry’s legacy but also introduces a fresh, instrumental dimension to his artistic output, appealing to fans of both his earlier work and the broader acid jazz genre.

The Matt Berry Trio’s sound is characterized by its intricate instrumental arrangements and Berry’s distinctive guitar work, which anchors the trio’s dynamic interplay with Scragg and Mann. Their music draws inspiration from a wide range of sources, including modern classical compositions and electronic textures, creating a rich and layered sonic experience that defines their contribution to the acid jazz movement. As the first album from the Matt Berry Trio, Everything’s Peachy establishes the group as a significant force in contemporary UK acid jazz, blending tradition with innovation in a way that resonates with both longtime fans and new listeners.

artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

artists.biography:
Graham Mann is a British singer/songwriter and multi-instrumentalist best known as a long-time collaborator of the renowned artist Matt Berry. Mann has worked closely with Berry on numerous projects, including the 2026 album Everything’s Peachy, released under the Matt Berry Trio, where he joined Berry and fellow collaborator Phill Scragg. His musical contributions span piano, trombone, and other instruments, and he has been credited on several of Berry’s works, including Are You Being Served, London Weekend Television, and Open University.

As a singer/songwriter, Mann brings a distinctive voice to the collaborative jazz, modern classical, and electronic soundscapes that define the Matt Berry Trio’s output. His partnership with Berry reflects a deep artistic synergy, with Mann often serving as a key creative force in shaping the trio’s leftward musical turn away from traditional songwriting toward more experimental and instrumental compositions. Mann’s versatility and musical depth have made him an integral part of Berry’s evolving artistic journey, particularly in the trio’s exploration of jazz and electronic influences.

While Mann’s solo work remains less documented in public sources, his significance within the broader context of Matt Berry’s musical universe is well established. His role as a trusted collaborator underscores his reputation as a skilled and adaptable musician who enhances the sonic richness of Berry’s projects. Through his work with the Matt Berry Trio and other collaborations, Graham Mann continues to contribute meaningfully to the contemporary landscape of British singer/songwriter and experimental music.

perplexity.description:
Everything's Peachy" by the Matt Berry Trio is the second volume in Acid Jazz Records' "The Jazz Sessions" series, released on June 26, 2026, as a remarkable 12-part instrumental suite that marks an exciting leftward turn for Matt Berry. Joining long-time collaborators Phill Scragg and Graham Mann, Berry takes a break from his usual songwriting to explore his deep jazz, modern classical, and electronic influences. The album is a cohesive work that showcases the trio's versatility, moving away from Berry's typical comedic rock style into a more sophisticated and atmospheric jazz realm.

The suite is inspired by the story of Richard "Beebo" Russell, an American folk hero known as "the Sky King," who famously stole a large aircraft with no flight training, performed stunts, and crashed to his own demise; the album's title derives from Russell's response to air traffic control during the incident. Released on black vinyl, with an Acid Jazz-exclusive "Opaque Spring Green" color vinyl limited to 500 copies, as well as CD and digital formats, "Everything's Peachy" stands as a significant and unique entry in Berry's catalog, offering listeners a remarkable 12-part journey through his diverse musical inspirations.
